items.title: Profit Booking Snaps Four-Week Market Rally
items.summary: Indian equities experienced a notable correction following a strong four-week rally, with the market succumbing to profit-taking. Major indices retreated as investors locked in previous gains while awaiting upcoming GDP growth statistics. Meanwhile, global technology shares recovered and metals remained subdued.
items.why: Profit booking happens when traders sell assets to lock in gains after a rapid price increase, which often causes a short-term market pullback.

items.title: SEBI Aims to Speed Up Foreign Portfolio Onboarding
items.summary: The market regulator plans to overhaul its rulebook to accelerate capital inflows into the nation. Under the proposed changes, foreign portfolio investor onboarding time would be drastically reduced from several months down to just five business days. The initiative is part of broader efforts to streamline market access and support economic growth.
items.why: Faster onboarding removes bureaucratic hurdles for international institutional funds, encouraging greater foreign capital allocation into domestic markets.

items.title: Foreign Investors Allowed in Physical Commodity Contracts
items.summary: Regulatory authorities have revised their framework to permit foreign portfolio investors to trade in physically settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives. Previously, participation was strictly limited to cash-settled non-agricultural contracts and associated indices. This update expands the range of instruments accessible to international market participants.
items.why: Allowing physical settlement options broadens the scope of commodity trading strategies for overseas investors, potentially deepening market liquidity.

items.title: Bond Yields Rise Amid Oil Spike and Rate Hike Bets
items.summary: Government bonds saw a notable decline as surging oil prices and rising global yields weighed on sentiment. The benchmark bond yield climbed to 7.2650%, marking its highest level in a week. Investors are increasingly pricing in potential monetary tightening by central banks due to persistent inflationary pressures.
items.why: Bond prices move inversely to yields; when inflation expectations or borrowing costs rise, existing fixed-rate bonds lose appeal, pushing yields up.

items.title: Central Bank Restores Daily Cash Reserve Ratio Mandate
items.summary: Financial institutions face tighter liquidity conditions as the Reserve Bank restored the requirement to maintain 90 percent of the cash reserve ratio on a daily basis. This policy shift aims to manage short-term banking system liquidity more effectively. Banks must now carefully monitor their daily cash balances to meet the stricter compliance threshold.
items.why: The cash reserve ratio dictates the minimum deposit percentage banks must hold as reserves, directly influencing the money supply and banking liquidity.

items.title: Analysts Project Aggressive Rate Hike by Reserve Bank
items.summary: Financial analysts have adjusted their policy outlook, with prominent forecasting groups now anticipating a 50-basis-point interest rate increase in December. Rising inflation risks and external economic pressures have prompted expectations of stronger monetary action. Higher benchmark rates typically translate to increased borrowing costs for consumers and businesses.
items.why: Central banks use rate hikes to cool down rising inflation, though higher rates can also slow economic momentum and increase loan EMIs.

items.title: Wall Street Rebounds as Investors Buy Battered Tech Shares
items.summary: United States equities advanced as market participants returned following the Thanksgiving holiday break to acquire previously beaten-down artificial intelligence stocks. The Nasdaq 100 advanced by 1.5 percent and the S&P 500 rose by 1.1 percent during the session. Despite the daily recovery, major benchmarks remained on course for broader weekly adjustments.
items.why: Tech stock rebounds reflect shifting risk appetite on Wall Street, where growth-oriented sectors heavily influence overall index movements.

items.title: Precious Metals Mixed as Federal Reserve Outlook Persists
items.summary: Gold drifted lower while silver managed gains during holiday-thinned trading sessions as participants evaluated ongoing US monetary policy signals. Expectations regarding future central bank interest rate decisions continued to influence bullion valuations. Traders closely monitor macroeconomic indicators to gauge the timing of potential policy shifts.
items.why: Precious metals are sensitive to interest rate expectations because higher rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets.
